t: Home › What is Screen & Notification Dimmer?
x: Screen & Notification Dimmer draws a dark layer over your display so you can dim the screen below your phone’s normal minimum brightness. You choose how dark, and the app shows it as a percentage darker than Android’s lowest brightness. It is built for reading in bed, using a phone next to someone who is asleep, or checking a notification in a dark room without being hit by light. Key features Dims below minimum brightness - useful in a dark room where the lowest system setting still feels too bright Quick levels - 20, 40, 60 and 80 (or your own presets), or drag the slider to any value Free bedtime schedule - on at 10:30 PM and off at 6 AM by default; change the times and days Dim for - dim for 15, 30 or 60

t: Dim the notification bar › Why most dimmers can't reach the notification shade
x: Android lets apps draw over other apps with the "Display over other apps" permission (its technical name is TYPE_APPLICATION_OVERLAY ). For security, Android keeps that kind of window below the system's own surfaces. The status bar, the notification shade, Quick Settings, the keyboard and the lock screen are all drawn above it, and some screens, such as parts of the Settings app, hide ordinary overlays altogether. So an overlay dimmer, however dark it is, has a bright hole exactly where your notifications appear. There is one window type that sits higher: the Accessibility overlay. t: Edge slider › How the edge slider works

t: Auto-Dim › How Auto-Dim works
x: While dimming and Auto-Dim are both on, the app takes a screenshot through Android's Accessibility screenshot API several times a second. It shrinks each one to a tiny low-resolution grid and works out one number: how bright the content is. Bright content raises the dimming, dark content lowers it. The image is processed in memory and thrown away immediately. It is never saved, never written to storage and never sent anywhere. The readout in the app shows what it sees, for example "Following the screen · content is 72% bright now".

t: Auto-Dim › Settings you can adjust
x: Setting What it changes Strength How far the level moves between dark and bright content Reaction speed: Gentle, Medium or Fast How quickly it responds. Gentle avoids flicker during fast scrolling; Fast catches sudden flashes sooner

t: Auto-Dim › How it differs from auto-brightness
x: Android's adaptive brightness and apps such as Lux or Super Dim 's automatic mode respond to the room , using the light sensor. In a dark bedroom the room barely changes, so the sensor has nothing to react to. Auto-Dim responds to the content , which is what actually changes when a bright page opens. The two work well together: let the system handle the room, and let Auto-Dim handle the screen.

t: Auto-Dim › Limits, honestly
x: Android 11 or newer only. The screenshot API it relies on does not exist before Android 11. Battery. It samples many times a second, so it uses more battery than plain dimming. The app says this up front, and how much depends on the phone. Protected content. Some apps (banking apps and DRM video) block screenshots. Android may not hand over a usable screenshot there, so Auto-Dim may not react inside those apps. Beta. I am still tuning it on different phones. If it misbehaves on yours, write to support@bunkwise.in with your phone model.

t: Auto-Dim › How to turn it on
x: Go to the Automate tab and switch on Auto-Dim . Without Pro, tap Watch an ad for a 12-hour unlock. Allow the "Screen & Notification Dimmer - better dimming" Accessibility service when asked. Set Strength and Reaction speed, then open a mixed app such as a browser to see it respond. You can also toggle it with the AUTO button on the notification or under the edge slider.

t: Auto-Dim › Frequently asked questions
x: Is there an app that dims bright white pages automatically? Yes. Auto-Dim in Screen & Notification Dimmer raises the dimming when the content on screen turns bright and lowers it when the content is dark. It needs Android 11 or newer. Does Auto-Dim record my screen? No. It reduces each screenshot to a single brightness number in memory and discards the image immediately. Nothing is saved or sent. Why does Auto-Dim not react in my banking app? Apps that block screenshots may not give Android's screenshot API a usable image, so Auto-Dim may not react there. Give those apps a fixed per-app level instead.

Default Press Volume Up + Volume Down together No Off, turn on in Emergency escape (needs the Accessibility service) Shake the phone firmly No Off, turn on in Emergency escape or from the Shake tile on Home Tap OFF on the notification A little Always available Tap the on/off Quick Settings tile A little Always available Turn off in the app Yes Always available When an escape fires, the app tells you what happened ("You pressed Volume Up + Down together") so it never looks like a crash.

t: Emergency off › Why both are off by default
x: Shake used to be on from the start. The trouble is that a phone carried in a pocket or bag gets shaken too, and the dimming would vanish for no visible reason. Pressing both volume keys also happens by accident, for example when you grab the phone in bed. A dimmer that switches itself off unasked feels broken, so both escapes are now opt-in. Turn on whichever suits you the first time you set the app up.

t: Emergency off › Adjusting the shake
x: Shake has a strength setting. If it fires while you walk, make it firmer; if it never fires, make it lighter. The volume combination is more precise and works inside any app, so it is the better choice if you can allow the Accessibility service.

t: Emergency off › A safety cap on darkness
x: Even at 100 the dark layer is not fully opaque. It stops at 97%, so on most phones you can still make out the screen in a dark room. That is deliberate. A fully black overlay would look exactly like a phone that has switched off.

t: Emergency off › Is this unusual?
x: Shake-to-disable is fairly common. Penumbra and Super Dim both list it. The volume-button combination is less common. I didn't find it in the listings of the other dimmers I compared, and it is the one I would pick, because it works without any guesswork.

t: Emergency off › Frequently asked questions

Otherwise pull down from the top of the screen and tap OFF on the dimmer notification or tap the on/off tile. Restarting the phone also clears the overlay, unless keep-after-restart is on. Is shake to turn off on by default? No. In current versions both shake and the volume-button escape are off until you switch them on under Settings > Emergency escape. Can the screen go completely black? No. The dark layer is capped at 97% opacity, so the screen stays faintly visible.

x: A free bedtime schedule that dims the screen for you By Madhav Raj , who builds Screen & Notification Dimmer · Updated 25 November 2026 · 2 min read Short answer Screen & Notification Dimmer can turn dimming on and off by itself every night. Open the Automate tab, switch on Night auto-dim , and choose the times and days. The default is 10:30 PM to 6:00 AM, every day. The schedule is free, with no ads and no trial. If you have to remember to switch the dimmer on, you will forget on the nights you need it. A schedule fixes that: the screen is already dark when you pick the phone up in bed, and back to normal in the morning.

t: Bedtime schedule (free) › How to set it up
x: Open the app and go to Automate > Schedule . Switch on Night auto-dim . Set the on time and the off time. The app shows how long that is, for example "Dimming for 7h 30m a night, every day". Under Repeat on , choose every day, weekdays, weekends or any set of days. The 24-hour strip at the top shows the dimmed window, so overnight times such as 11 PM to 7 AM are easy to check.

t: Bedtime schedule (free) › How accurate is the timing?
x: The schedule fires within a couple of minutes of the time you set, even when the phone is in Doze. To-the-second timing would need Android's exact alarm permission, and I chose not to ask for it, because a dimmer doesn't need it. If you open the phone exactly at 10:30, give it a minute. If you set the on and off times to the same value, the app warns you that nothing will happen. If no days are ticked, it says the schedule will never fire.

t: Bedtime schedule (free) › Making it reliable on Xiaomi, Samsung and others
x: Some phone makers stop background apps more aggressively than stock Android, and that can stop a schedule from firing.
